default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-099.title: Round-number rejection
E-099.hypothesis: Retail and discretionary WIN traders anchor take-profits, limit entries and option strikes on round index levels (multiples of 250/500/1000 points), so resting liquidity clusters there; the first bar that reaches the level from below and closes back under it shows that liquidity absorbing the push, so fade away from it.

E-100.title: Prior-session POC rejection
E-100.hypothesis: Yesterday's point of control (the price bin with the most volume) is where the largest share of yesterday's inventory was built; those holders defend their cost, so the first touch of it from one side that closes back on that side meets their orders and price moves away from the level.

E-101.title: Morning/evening star after a run
E-101.hypothesis: A large bar making the lowest close of a run, followed by a small indecision bar and then a bar closing back above the large bar's body midpoint, shows the run's last burst found no follow-through and buyers retook half its ground; the late sellers of the burst are trapped, so follow the three-bar reversal (mirror).

E-102.title: Choppiness-index trend onset
E-102.hypothesis: Dreiss' Choppiness Index compares the summed true range to the net high-low span; after a choppy stretch (above 61.8) a fall below a low threshold means the bars have started to line up in one direction, i.e. the balance broke and one side is now initiating; follow the direction of the window's move.

E-103.title: Late-session intraday momentum (first-window sign)
E-103.hypothesis: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou: the market's first half-hour return from the prior close predicts the last half-hour, because institutional rebalancing and informed orders delayed to the close trade the same way; in the closing window, enter in the sign of the opening return whenever price is on that side of a short EMA.

E-104.title: Volume-climax stall fade
E-104.hypothesis: At the end of a run, the bar with the highest volume of the window (and far above normal for its minute) is the buying climax where the last chasers and stops are filled; when the next bar trades much less, fails to extend and closes below the climax close, demand is spent, so fade the run (mirror for a selling climax).

E-105.title: Raschke Anti stochastic hook
E-105.hypothesis: Raschke's 'Anti': the slow %D sets the momentum trend, the fast %K pulls back toward it and then hooks back in the trend direction; the hook marks the end of the counter-trend correction, when trend traders re-enter and the correction traders cover, so follow the hook (mirror).

E-106.title: Hoffman inventory retracement bar
E-106.hypothesis: In a steep EMA trend, a bar whose open and close sit at least 45% below its high is counter-trend inventory being worked by short-term sellers while institutions pause; a close above that bar's high within three bars shows the counter-trend selling is done and the trend side resumes, so follow it (mirror).

E-107.title: Previous clock-hour extreme rejection
E-107.hypothesis: Hourly candles are what most desks and chart traders read, so the completed previous hour's high and low hold resting orders and take-profits; the first bar of the session that pokes through such a level and closes back inside meets that liquidity and the poke's buyers are trapped, so fade back into the hour's range.

E-108.title: Williams squat-bar break
E-108.hypothesis: Bill Williams' squat bar (volume up while range per contract falls) is a standoff where heavy two-sided trade makes no progress; whichever side then closes beyond the squat bar's range within a few bars has absorbed the other, whose stops sit just beyond it, so follow the break.
